page.layout: One main text column; in the right margin, beside the lines of the second paragraph, one side note of four lines. Running head at top, page number at top right, signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: commendantur, illi enim excrementis abundant. Opimantur loco tenebroso, & tepido caueis conclusi. Largioribus autem cibariis opus est & largiori potu, voracitas enim in iis eximia est & bibendi desiderium ingens: atque sic bene curati, duobus ad summum mensibus alii prepinguescunt, euadunt Castaneis, pyrijs, malis, & id genus alijs ad farcturam idoneis solent farciri vetuli & adultiores, sic enim lautiores euadunt, pulli vero oleribus herbisq; ac lardo minutim concijo.

Ceruix, ala, pedes cum palmisIus anse-rum cō-tra vene-na effi-cax., pipere & vino solent elixari, idq; edulii genus prima mensa solet apponi palato gratissimum & saluberrimum, ius enim contra toxica & aconita efficax esse admodum, compertum habetur.

Ad extremum adipem anserum fartiliumJ celeberrimos vsus nobis præstare frigoribus hibernis in condienda brassica aliisque oleribus, sicut & aliis obsoniis parandis, omnibus culinis plusquam notum est, omitto nunc, quantum in re medica valeat, de quo hic meminisse nihil attinet.

page.notes: Printed side note in the right margin: "Ius anserum contra venena efficax", set with hyphens at the line ends. "fartilium" at the end of the third paragraph is doubtful, probably "farturiū" or similar, so I left it with a [?]-free reading but it should be checked. Marks in the text are not printed. The first word "atque" in the first paragraph is doubtful: the scan shows a short abbreviated form. "Opimantur" is read from a faint scan. Running head "PROROGANDA" is letter-spaced.
